metric.why: Distributed AI training is unusually intolerant of network degradation; a lossy fabric shows up as wasted GPU-hours before it shows up as an outage.
metric.metric: Network latency, packet loss, and bandwidth
metric.definition: Continuous measurement of round-trip latency, loss rate, and utilization on the facility's internal fabric and external transit.

reading.body:
Distributed AI training fails silently under network degradation long before it fails loudly as an outage, making latency and packet loss metrics leading indicators of wasted compute.

Data centers measure their internal network fabric and external connections continuously for latency, loss rate, and utilization because these metrics detect GPU inefficiency faster than traditional monitoring does. A lossy network looks like slow training to the user, but register as hardware sitting idle or moving corrupted data to the cluster. For AI workloads that span hundreds or thousands of GPUs, even brief packet loss or high latency compounds across parallel tasks and synchronization points.

This metric tracks operations rather than incidents, which reflects a shift in how infrastructure reliability works for AI. The old data center model flagged outages after users noticed them. The new model catches degradation before training jobs stall or restart. It does not directly measure power consumption or building capacity, but poor network health forces the power plant to cool hardware that produces nothing, turning a transmission problem into a consumption problem.
